s1.syndrome_frame: Postpartum headache with worsening course and associated symptoms
salient_findings: Layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection on noncontrast CT
key_facts: 31 days postpartum after elective cesarean delivery
Initial mild global headache developed 8 days postoperatively
Normal prothrombin time, partial prothrombin time, and international normalized ratio

raw.syndrome_frame: Postpartum headache with worsening course and associated symptoms
salient_findings: Layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection on noncontrast CT
key_facts: 31 days postpartum after elective cesarean delivery
Initial mild global headache developed 8 days postoperatively
Normal prothrombin time, partial prothrombin time, and international normalized ratio

shortlist.label: Subdural hematoma
shortlist.why_kept: Layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection on CT

shortlist.label: Chronic subdural hematoma
shortlist.why_kept: Delayed onset and worsening of headache

shortlist.label: Spontaneous intracranial hypotension
shortlist.why_kept: Post-dural puncture headache is a possibility given spinal anesthesia

shortlist.label: Epidural hematoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, cannot be ruled out without further imaging

raw.rationale: The patient's worsening headache over time, particularly the progression from a mild to a severe headache, along with the presence of a layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection on the noncontrast CT of the head, is consistent with a chronic subdural hematoma, which can develop after a traumatic event like a cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia.

rejected.label: Subdural hematoma
rejected.why: While possible, the chronic nature of the symptoms and the specific imaging findings better support a chronic rather than an acute subdural hematoma.

rejected.label: Spontaneous intracranial hypotension
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with postural headaches, which is not the case here as the headache is described as nonpositional.

rejected.label: Reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome
rejected.why: The absence of thunderclap headache and the specific imaging findings do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis
rejected.why: Normal vital signs, lack of specific neurological deficits, and the nature of the headache do not align well with this condition.

rejected.label: Postpartum cerebral angiopathy
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and imaging findings do not specifically suggest this condition, which is more associated with thunderclap headaches and vasculitis.

rejected.label: Spinal headache
rejected.why: Although the patient had a spinal anesthesia, the headache's characteristics and the imaging findings are not typical for a spinal headache, which is usually postural.

rejected.label: Epidural hematoma
rejected.why: The imaging description of a layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection is more consistent with a subdural than an epidural hematoma, which typically appears as a biconvex or lentiform-shaped hyperdensity on CT.
